lines.text: If you have an unused fifty-dollar gift card to a retail store that files for bankruptcy, is your money gone?
The brutal legal reality is that gift card holders are considered unsecured creditors.
When a company files Chapter 11 bankruptcy, federal courts freeze operations to pay major lenders first.
The retailer must request special permission from the bankruptcy judge to continue accepting gift cards.
If the company shifts to total liquidation, gift card redemptions are terminated instantly.
You can file a formal claim with the bankruptcy court, but cardholders typically receive only pennies on the dollar years later.
Always spend gift cards as soon as you receive them rather than stashing them in a drawer.
